common_name: Cast in Bronze Distylium (Coppery New-Growth Southern Living Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, organically enriched soil in full sun to part shade; its naturally rounded, gracefully arching form needs minimal corrective pruning to keep a tidy foundation or hedge shape.

directions: Cast in Bronze is a Southern Living Plant Collection distylium selection whose flush of new foliage emerges a coppery bronze-maroon before maturing to glossy dark green, giving the shrub seasonal color shifts on top of its year-round evergreen structure. Its dense, naturally rounded habit with gently arching branch tips suits foundation plantings, low hedges, and mixed borders where a boxwood or holly substitute is needed in humid, wet-soil-prone Southern gardens. It tolerates both full sun and part shade, adapts to average to wet garden soil, and shrugs off deer browsing and summer heat. Prune lightly after the main growth flush if a tighter form is desired, since the plant otherwise holds its shape with little maintenance.
sources: Southern Living Plant Collection product page

common_name: Bayou Bliss Distylium (Fine-Textured Blue-Green Southern Living Evergreen Shrub, formerly Jewel Box)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, average garden soil in full sun to part shade; its low, wide-spreading habit fits borders and low foundation plantings better than taller distylium selections.

directions: Bayou Bliss is a low, wide Southern Living Plant Collection distylium prized for its fine-textured, soft blue-green evergreen foliage and compact, rounded form, making it a useful boxwood or holly alternative for borders and low foundation beds. It carries the genus's small, inconspicuous reddish late-winter flowers without seed litter, and its wetland-adapted parentage lets it tolerate both average and periodically soggy soil far better than many broadleaf evergreens. Grow it in full sun to part shade and expect minimal disease or deer pressure once established. Light shearing after the spring growth flush keeps the naturally tidy habit even more uniform, though it needs little pruning to look good.
sources: Southern Living Plant Collection product page

common_name: Miss Scarlett Illicium (Compact Crimson-Flowered Florida Anise, Southern Living Plant Collection)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in part shade to full shade; its more compact frame than the species suits smaller shade beds and foundation plantings.

directions: Miss Scarlett is a Southern Living Plant Collection selection of native Florida anise bred to stay noticeably more compact than the wild species while still producing its signature star-shaped, strap-petaled crimson flowers each spring. Its glossy, anise-scented evergreen foliage releases fragrance when brushed or crushed, and the dense, upright habit provides reliable year-round screening in shaded woodland gardens or foundation beds. It thrives in the moist, humus-rich, part-to-full-shade conditions of a Gulf South understory planting and, like the species, is deer resistant and largely trouble-free. Give it consistent moisture and minimal pruning beyond removing any winter dieback to keep its naturally dense form intact.

common_name: Tokyo Skies Aspidistra (Cream-and-White Variegated Cast Iron Plant, Southern Living Plant Collection)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container perennials in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in part to full shade with only morning sun; strong direct sun scorches leaves and fades the cream-and-white variegation.

directions: Tokyo Skies is a Southern Living Plant Collection cast iron plant selected for broad, arching leaves splashed with irregular cream and white variegation over a dark green background, a bolder and more painterly pattern than the fine speckling of older cast iron cultivars. Like other Aspidistra elatior selections it is extremely tough and drought-tolerant once established, making it a dependable groundcover under trees or along shaded walkways where little else will grow. Keep it out of prolonged direct sun, which scorches the foliage and dulls its variegation, and divide congested clumps in spring if a wider planting is wanted. It needs almost no fertilizing or pest management in the deep, humus-rich shade it prefers.
sources: Southern Living Plant Collection product page
Plant Development Services / Sunset Plant Collection (Cultivate'23 Retailers' Choice Award)

common_name: Early Wonder Camellia (Early-Fall-Blooming Lavender-Pink Formal Double, Southern Living Plant Collection)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5-6.5), humus-rich soil with 3-4 hours of direct sun or all-day filtered light; its unusually early fall bloom window sets it apart from most Camellia japonica cultivars, which flower in winter.

directions: Early Wonder is a Southern Living Plant Collection japonica camellia notable for opening its formal double, lavender-pink blooms in early fall, well ahead of the winter-to-spring bloom season typical of most Camellia japonica cultivars. Its dark green, leathery, lightly serrated evergreen foliage provides structure year-round, and the early flowering window extends color into a season when few other shade shrubs are blooming. Give it dappled or filtered light, since only a few hours of direct sun are needed, along with consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil and a mulch layer to protect its shallow roots. Prune only lightly right after flowering finishes so the following year's flower buds are not removed.
sources: Southern Living Plant Collection product page

common_name: Purple Daydream Loropetalum (Compact Reblooming Purple-Leaf Fringe Flower, Southern Living Plant Collection)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to dappled part shade; a spring application of slow-release, acidic fertilizer helps sustain its deep purple leaf color.

directions: Purple Daydream is a compact Southern Living Plant Collection loropetalum holding purple-to-dark-purple foliage year-round on a tidy, low-mounding frame, with dark pink, ribbon-like flowers opening heavily in spring and sporadically reappearing through the growing season. Its smaller stature compared to older loropetalum cultivars suits accent plantings, low hedges, mass plantings, and large containers without the frequent shearing bigger selections need. It adapts to full sun for the richest color or dappled part shade in hotter climates, and appreciates well-drained soil amended for slight acidity. Minimal pruning right after the main spring flush is all that is needed to keep its naturally compact habit dense.
sources: Southern Living Plant Collection product page

common_name: Gatsby Glow Ball Oakleaf Hydrangea (Compact Ball-Flowered Native Oakleaf)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade (4-6 hours of light); its compact 3-4 foot frame and quicker finishing time make it well suited to smaller beds and container production.

directions: Gatsby Glow Ball is a compact oakleaf hydrangea bred by Dr. Tom Ranney at NC State, producing dense, rounded, ball-shaped flower heads instead of the elongated panicles typical of the species, opening crisp white and aging to a soft glowing green. Its oversized, deeply lobed leaves turn burgundy-red in fall, giving multi-season interest on a shrub compact enough for foundation plantings, groupings, or woodland edges where full-sized oakleaf hydrangeas would outgrow the space. It tolerates part shade better than most panicle-type hydrangeas and benefits from afternoon shade in hot climates to prevent leaf scorch. Prune only right after flowering, since next year's buds form on the current season's growth.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox (Hydrangea quercifolia Gatsby Glow Ball 'NCHQ1')

common_name: Fairytrail Fresco Cascade Hydrangea (Trailing Mophead Hydrangea with Every-Node Blooms)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil with 4-6 hours of sun and protected morning shade; too much afternoon sun burns the foliage and reduces bloom quality on this cascade-habit selection.

directions: Fairytrail Fresco is a cascade-habit hydrangea that sets mophead flower buds at every leaf node along its trailing stems, creating a garland-like curtain of blue or pink blooms (color shifting with soil pH) rather than flowers concentrated only at stem tips. It blooms earlier than most hydrangeas and its foliage turns red in fall, extending seasonal interest on a compact, cloud-shaped plant well suited to containers, hanging baskets, or the front edge of a shaded border. Give it morning sun with afternoon shade, since more than about six hours of direct sun scorches its leaves and reduces flowering and stem strength. It needs only light shaping and consistent moisture to keep its cascading form full.
sources: Proven Winners ColorChoice product page (Fairytrail Fresco Cascade Hydrangea)
